doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Farm inheritance, the general store and service station
summary: The farm passed to the sons; the family also owned the Tippo general store and service station.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your father inherit the farm from your grandfather, or was it... I gather from an interview that your grandfather married three times, and that your father was from the second marriage. So I’m wondering how the farm came to him...
Well, my uncle and my father inherited the farm.
He also had five daughters who didn’t inherit the farm. That’s how it was then.
So it got passed down to the males.
But I gather your father had other interests as well. He liked music and he had a player piano.
Yes. He had a general store in Tippo, and... I think my grandfather had that originally, but it passed down to my father.
So he had the store that everyone in the community would come to purchase provisions. Was it like a commissary store?
It was sort of a focal point. But it was across the street from the service station.
Yes. Those two places were... In fact, I think that Mose’s mother always said that the men gathered at the service station.
So your family owned the general store and the service station, and a 1400-acre farm.
Yes. It was pretty much that...you know...
